newsitem.title: FRANCE: ALPINE SKIING-WOMEN'S GIANT SLALOM STOPPED IN MORZINE.
newsitem.headline: ALPINE SKIING-WOMEN'S GIANT SLALOM STOPPED IN MORZINE.

text.p: A women's World Cup Alpine skiing giant slalom was stopped after 19 starters on Sunday because of the dangerous condition of the snow.
Organisers, who put back the start of the race three times, decided to call it a day when Italian Barbara Merlin fell on a course made much too soft by warm weather.
Products used to harden the snow also proved inefficient despite a delay of more than two-and-a-half hours.
A power breakdown and fog also hampered the race and, after watering the piste and putting salt on it to no effect, stewards from the International Ski Federation (FIS) decided to halt the first leg.
Austrian veteran Anita Wachter had clocked a fastest time of one minute and 15.02 seconds when the race was stopped but the times looked rather irrelevant because of the poor state of the snow.
Gaps between skiers had been unusually high for a giant slalom.

While world champion Deborah Compagnoni managed to limit the damage to 0.30 seconds, specialists such as Italian Sabina Panzanini, winner of the last giant slalom held in Parck City, Utah, last month, or World Cup holder Katja Seizinger were trailing Wachter by more than two seconds.
Swiss prospect Karin Roten was third fastest on 1:15.83.
It was the second women's giant slalom to be rescheduled this season. The race due to take place in nearby Val d'Isere 10 days ago could go ahead either. It will be held in Zwiesel in mid-January.
There was no immediate hint at when Sunday's race might be re-run.
"It was the right decision to stop the race," said France's Leila Piccard, one of the 19 skiers who were allowed to start.

"The bottom part was all right but the top was deteriorating quickly. What's more, we had been up sincel five in the morning for a 0930 start and we were getting tired," said Piccard, who had finished fourth in a slalom in Crans Montana, Switzerland, on Saturday.
Skiers now have a short break for Christmas before going to Siemmering, Austria, for two slaloms on December 28 and 29.
A downhill and a combined which were to take place in Crans Montana on Friday and Saturday also had to be scrapped because of rain.
